scope: Investigate witnessed AC1018 TABLE 528 merge geometry and omitted cell-level top-border visibility; no implementation or native semantic claim.

sources.custody: Existing external repository samples used read-only; file naming, handle and selected field agreement do not establish common save state or native producer.

oda.observed: For DWG up to R21, 175 and 176 represent horizontal and vertical counts of merged cells; 173 indicates a cell merged with another. The text does not explicitly establish anchor-versus-covered polarity. A 0x04000 override has a top visibility BS field, where 1 is visible. Shared/virtual edge properties require the adjacent-cell context. No omitted-DXF-289 default is specified here.

authority.autodeskDistinction: The TABLE DXF reference identifies a cell-level 289 visibility flag without an omitted default. Its default of 1 for 284–289 is explicitly table-entity-level; it does not establish the cell-level default.

mergePattern.inference: The physical pattern suggests two rectangular anchor/covered relationships. The pattern alone and ODA wording do not establish the producer’s merge polarity or native geometry.

typedProbe.result: Original ASCII DXF imports with semanticComplete=false and seven 1×1 m_mergedRanges at the covered-cell positions; it does not publish the two suggested rectangles. Writer preflight rejects unmerged spans greater than one, so the source anchor is refused instead of silently normalized.

borderVisibility.flagMeaning: 0x4460 includes text height, top-border color, top-border lineweight and top-border visibility according to the ODA DWG flag table. The color value is retained as a 16-bit DXF group; do not infer full RGB semantics.

copyProbe.result: Both original DXF encodings yield selected typed cell mask=17504, height=4, top weight=40, top color=63 and current library default top visible=true. Copied into an otherwise exportable authored 1×1 table, the full profile is atomically refused; changing mask to 0x20 and clearing the two border fields succeeds on the same exporter. This is a selected copied-cell diagnostic, not a full original output.

pairReadback.result: Ordinary ACadSharp reads of the paired-named DWG and ASCII DXF report the same handle, 7×3 shape, and selected text, edge and merge-span values. For cell 18, its DWG read reports top-invisible=true; its DXF read reports false, but that DXF reader ignores 289 and returns its own default. Its DWG visibility branch wrongly tests the 0x400 lineweight flag rather than 0x4000; both bits are set in the corresponding DXF profile, but independent raw-bit and common-save-state proof remain missing.

libredwg.result: dwgread reports process success but represents DWG handle 528 as UNKNOWN_OBJ; it does not decode cell visibility.

experimentalTrace.result: A scratch-only instrumented reader observes mask 0x40020 at the first DWG table cell, which the production unknown-bit guard refuses. An intentionally guard-bypassed diagnostic reaches cell 12 but reports invalid visibility 256 and does not reliably reach cell 18; it is likely desynchronized and is not a raw visibility proof. No production guard was modified.
